doc.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018

title: Pittsburgh trombone scene: Harold Betters, Al Dow and Slide Hampton
summary: Harold Betters is still playing; Al Dow's jam session welcomed Watkins from Wheeling, and Harold and Slide Hampton were recently interviewed together.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Let’s talk about Pittsburgh for a moment.

I have this — when we started this project back in 1995, I remember someone saying, “Well you should go interview Harold Betters, the world’s loudest trombone player.” I said, “Really? The world’s loudest trombone player.” He was a Pittsburgh —
He’s still there. We just had a birthday celebration for him. Lots of the trombone players came out, the guys from the symphony, local trombone players, and there’s Harold, in his nineties.

He’s still playing. They just had Slide Hampton in Pittsburgh about a month ago and there they had Harold Betters and Al Dow, another local trombone player in Pittsburgh, who is one of the first people that allowed me to come up and sit in and be receptive to us. We couldn’t play you know. I’m from Wheeling, West Virginia originally so the big city to us was Pittsburgh. We would drive up, go to Al Dow’s jam session and then drive back to West Virginia you know. And Al would let us on stage. He would welcome us into the community. But Harold, yeah, so they just had Slide there and Peter Lynne, are you familiar with Peter Lynne the trombonist? He plays trombone. He helps Slide. You know Slide had a stroke not long ago so he helps Slide with some things, some physical things and also some musical things so they brought them out to Pittsburgh for the show, and he did a great interview of Slide and Harold. This was just a month ago so you can find that on line, there’s Slide and Harold talking about each other sitting next to each other.
Yeah. That’s a great thing to capture.

And Harold said, “I could never play fast like these guys so I just play melodies.” And Slide said, “I couldn’t play melodies, so I just played fast.” Just to see the two of them sitting there, it was great.
